network.name: Arc Testnet
network.note: Testnet only. Arc's public mainnet launches 2026-09-16, three days after this project's 2026-09-13 ETHOnline submission deadline — see mainnetRequirements below. Native gas currency is USDC itself (shown with 18 decimals at the protocol level; the ERC-20 USDC contract below still reports 6 decimals, like every other chain's USDC).

source.treeCleanAtDeployNote: Deployed with script/DeployArcTestnet.s.sol, test/DeployArcTestnet.t.sol and this README update uncommitted at deploy time (all net-new, additive files — no uncommitted change to TouchstoneAttestation.sol/TouchstoneEscrow.sol themselves, which are unmodified from gitCommit above). Recorded honestly rather than claiming a clean-tree deploy that didn't happen — same practice as base-sepolia.json.

compiler.evmVersionRationale: PUSH0 is universally available but Cancun opcodes are not; shanghai is the portable floor that already kept Arc a deployment target rather than a rewrite — see CLAUDE.md and foundry.toml's own comment on this.

reuses.note: Same deployer EOA and same TOUCHSTONE_PUBLISHER_KEY as the Base Sepolia deployment (data/deployments/base-sepolia.json) — testnet-only, no security consequence, and it means the same key that signs a print anchors it on both chains.

usdc.source: Circle official documentation, resolved via Circle's MCP server on 2026-09-05
corroboration: packages/sdk/src/money/assets.ts's arc-testnet entry — added speculatively before this deployment, now independently verified correct rather than merely trusted
usdc.verifiedOnChain: balanceOf(deployer) queried live via cast before deployment returned a nonzero real balance (40999579 minor units), confirming the address is a live, funded ERC-20 contract on this chain, not just a documented one

verified.note: Confirmed via Blockscout's own API (GET /api/v2/smart-contracts/<address> → is_verified: true), not just the submission response — forge verify-check returned a stale/racy result immediately after submission for the sibling Escrow contract below, so the API was checked directly as ground truth for both.

TouchstoneAttestation.notes: Same publisher key as Base Sepolia's TouchstoneAttestation (compressed pubkey 0x030c598ee35bd24b6942e9155bd36c1dbbe77936c700f859e75b0168b0e25cb299) — the key that signs a print anchors it on both chains. Immutable: rotating the publisher means deploying a new instance.

verified.note: See TouchstoneAttestation.verified.note above — the same forge verify-check timing caveat applied here, resolved the same way.

TouchstoneEscrow.feeBpsMeaning: 50 basis points = 0.50%, charged on actualAmount only and deducted from seller proceeds. Contract cap MAX_FEE_BPS = 100 (1%). Same as Base Sepolia's own configuration.
TouchstoneEscrow.notes: treasury and feeBps are immutable with no setter. Treasury here is the deployer EOA, acceptable on testnet only — same choice as Base Sepolia.

mainnetRequirements: treasury MUST be a Safe/multisig, not an EOA. It is immutable with no setter, so a lost key makes fee revenue permanently unrecoverable and the only remedy is redeploying the escrow and migrating every integrator.
Generate TOUCHSTONE_PUBLISHER_KEY on an air-gapped machine. The testnet key reused here has passed through repository-adjacent files.
DeployArcTestnet.s.sol is chain-guarded to 5042002; a mainnet deployment needs its own script and its own review.

Arc mainnet's own chain ID and USDC contract address must be independently re-verified against Circle's/Arc's own documentation at deploy time — never copied from this testnet record, even though Arc's testnet USDC happens to sit at a distinctive, memorable address (0x3600...0000).

Arc's public mainnet launches 2026-09-16 — see packages/contracts/script/DeployArcMainnet.s.sol, prepared but not run, with its chain-id guard deliberately left as an env-var placeholder rather than a guessed constant.

1_anchorRealPrint.description: Reused Base Sepolia's own worked-example body hash (docs/siu-worked-example.md), anchored on this separate contract instance via a direct postPrint call from TOUCHSTONE_PUBLISHER_KEY. Confirmed isPosted(bodyHash) == true, publisher() matches the expected address, and a second postPrint of the same hash reverts.

2_buyerSellerWorkerLoop.description: The full Phase-E deliverable: two real Cloudflare Worker sellers (packages/agents/src/workers/seller.ts, deployed as touchstone-arc-seller-a/b) and a real Worker buyer (workers/buyer.ts, touchstone-arc-buyer) run the complete discover→quote→compare→fund→settle→verify loop end to end, real HTTP, real chain, real inference, real Circle-Gateway-free verify_receipt against the isolated arc-testbed MCP Worker. Ran successfully via POST https://touchstone-arc-buyer.perklur.workers.dev/run.

3_escrowLifecycleLiveTest.description: packages/agents/src/arc.live.test.ts — the same suite live.test.ts already runs against Base Sepolia, ported to Arc: real openAndFund, real readEscrowUntilMatch, real settle, real LocalSettlementReader read bound by quote hash, and a real rejection of a quote that doesn't hash to what was actually settled. Ran with ARC_TESTNET_RPC_URL=https://rpc.drpc.testnet.arc.io — all 4 tests passed for real, no mocks.

notSeparatelyReRunOnArc.note: escrowExpiryReclaim, quoteHashNotReusable (the funding-side, non-verify_receipt version), and the feeFloorBoundaries sweep (99/100/199/1000) are not independently re-verified live on this deployment. TouchstoneEscrow's bytecode here is identical to Base Sepolia's (same source, same compiler/optimizer settings — see compiler above and noAdminPathCheckedOnLiveBytecode below), that exact behaviour is already exhaustively covered by 92 passing Foundry unit/fuzz/invariant tests (chain-independent by construction — they exercise the contract's own logic, not network conditions) and was already live-smoke-tested once, on the same bytecode, on Base Sepolia (base-sepolia.json's own smokeTests 3/4/5). Re-running the identical boundary arithmetic against identical bytecode on a second chain would mostly re-prove the Solidity compiler behaves the same way twice, not surface anything Arc-specific — the two chain-specific things worth checking for real (gas economics, RPC quirks, verify_receipt's chain-name gating) are exactly what smokeTests 2 and 3 above exercised, and both surfaced real, previously-unknown platform differences (Arc's real gas price required raising this session's seller funding amounts; the primary RPC endpoint rate-limited under sustained traffic, worked around with dRPC's documented mirror; Worker-to-Worker fetch() to a bare *.workers.dev URL is blocked by Cloudflare, worked around with custom domains).

noAdminPathCheckedOnLiveBytecode.note: Structural property of the compiled bytecode, chain-independent — test/NoAdminPath.t.sol already asserts this from the ABI/bytecode itself and applies identically here since the contracts are byte-for-byte the same as Base Sepolia's deployment.
